Answer: (a, c)

Solution:

The correct answer is (c) Live because x is used in subsequent iterations.

Here's why, based on the principles of live variable analysis in compiler optimization:

Live Variable Analysis

Live variable analysis is a backward data-flow analysis that determines, for each program point, which variables hold values that may be used later in the program.

  • A variable V is live at a program point P if there is a path from P to a use of V that does not pass through any definition (assignment) of V.
  • Otherwise, V is dead.

Analysis of the Loop

The code snippet is:

while (...) {

    x = x + 1;  // <-- This is the assignment in question

}

x = 100;

Let's focus on the assignment x = x + 1; inside the loop body.

  1. Use of x: The expression x + 1 uses the current value of x.
  2. Subsequent Use: In the very next iteration of the while loop (if the loop condition is still true), the value produced by the assignment (x = x + 1;) will be used again on the right-hand side of the same assignment statement.
  3. Conclusion: The value assigned to x in any iteration is immediately needed (and therefore live) for the calculation in the next iteration.

Therefore, the assignment to x in the loop body is Live because x is used in subsequent iterations.

·         (a) Live because x is the part of Out-set of basic block: In the loop body, the statement defines x (new value) and that new value is needed in the next iteration (because the next iteration evaluates x = x + 1 again, using the current x on the RHS).

·         In liveness terms, because of the back edge to the loop, x is in the OUT set of the loop-body basic block.

·         (b) Not live because x is assigned a value after loop: The assignment x = 100; after the loop kills any previous value of x at that point. However, this is irrelevant to the liveness of x inside the loop for its own iterative computation.

(d) Live because x is the part of In-set of basic block: The In-set is the set of variables live upon entry to the block. x will be in the In-set because it's used inside the block, but again, option (c) is the best description of the cause of its liveness for this specific assignment.

Now check whether A → ε also goes into M[A, e]. That happens only if e ∈ FOLLOW(A).

Compute FOLLOW(A) quickly:

  • From S → b S d A, A is at the end ⇒ FOLLOW(A) ⊇ FOLLOW(S)

  • FOLLOW(S) contains $ (start symbol) and also from A → e S c, S is followed by c ⇒ c ∈ FOLLOW(S), and from S → b S d A, S is followed by d ⇒ d ∈ FOLLOW(S)
    So FOLLOW(S) = { $, c, d }

  • From B → bA, A is at end ⇒ FOLLOW(A) ⊇ FOLLOW(B)

  • From S → a B c d, B is followed by c ⇒ c ∈ FOLLOW(B); from B → b B a, B is followed by a ⇒ a ∈ FOLLOW(B)
    So FOLLOW(B) includes { c, a }

Hence:
FOLLOW(A) includes { $, c, d, a }
So e ∉ FOLLOW(A), therefore A → ε is NOT placed in M[A, e].
